analytes.label: Lead
analytes.remediation_note: Trace the highest-risk ingredient inputs (rice flour, root vegetables, cocoa, leafy greens, low-quality vitamin/mineral premixes) and request a recent ingredient-level COA before targeting the finished-product result.

analytes.label: Cadmium
analytes.remediation_note: Cadmium typically tracks soil and crop type (sunflower, cocoa, spinach, soy). Confirm sourcing region and rotate to lower-Cd ingredient suppliers where possible before pursuing in-process mitigation.

analytes.label: Arsenic (total)
analytes.remediation_note: Total arsenic includes the much-lower-risk organic forms; if the toxic inorganic fraction is the driver, request an iAs/tAs speciation result from the lab before deciding on mitigation steps.

analytes.label: Arsenic (inorganic)
analytes.remediation_note: Inorganic arsenic typically tracks rice and rice-derivatives (brown rice syrup, rice protein). Lower-iAs rice varieties (Californian, basmati) and rinse-and-cook protocols are the first levers; ingredient substitution is the strongest.

analytes.label: Mercury (total)
analytes.remediation_note: Total mercury is most informative for non-fish matrices; in fish or shellfish, request methylmercury speciation because that is the toxicologically active fraction and the regulated species.

analytes.label: Mercury (methyl)
analytes.remediation_note: Methylmercury is concentrated in larger predatory fish. The most direct lever is fish-species selection (smaller, shorter-lived species) rather than processing change.

analytes.label: Nickel
analytes.remediation_note: Nickel often migrates from stainless-steel processing equipment in acidic or chloride-rich matrices. Audit dwell time, equipment alloy grade, and ingredient-borne nickel (legumes, oats, soy) in that order.

analytes.label: Aluminum
analytes.remediation_note: Aluminum in food often tracks packaging contact, additives (sodium aluminum phosphates), and certain mineral premixes. Review the additive/premix supplier specs before pursuing process changes.

analytes.label: Chromium (hexavalent)
analytes.remediation_note: Hexavalent chromium is rarely reported in food; confirm the lab actually speciated Cr(VI) rather than reporting total chromium, because the two are not interchangeable for regulatory or toxicological purposes.

analytes.label: Tin
analytes.remediation_note: Tin in canned or metal-packaged products typically tracks can-coating wear and storage time; review packaging supplier specs, lacquer integrity, and shelf-life protocols.
